title: Spanish government says sorry to people of Ceuta for migrant crisis
summary:
The Spanish government has apologised to the people of Ceuta for the migrant crisis that has affected the city for weeks and it has unveiled plans to overhaul the country's immigration laws.
At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta, a Spanish exclave in North Africa on 30 and 31 July.
The vast majority of the migrants returned to Morocco within hours of their arrival, but several thousand remain in Ceuta, many of them children, and most sleeping rough on beaches or streets.
The Sánchez government has now declared a situation of interest for national security in the city, centralising management of the crisis.
Territorial Policy Minister Ángel Víctor Torres has been tasked with co-ordinating the response, relieving the Ceuta local government of that responsibility.

title: Fentanyl investigations dropped during Trump’s immigration crackdown, DHS watchdog says
summary:
The Department of Homeland Security’s decision last year to pull additional federal agents for immigration enforcement resulted in a dramatic drop in fentanyl investigations and seizures by the department’s investigations division, according to a federal watchdog report.
The sudden change in approach toward ongoing fentanyl-related efforts stemmed from President Donald Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown, which required federal agents across the government to be pulled in for immigration arrests.
That included agents from Immigration and Customs Enforcement Homeland Security Investigations, the body charged with combatting cartels and criminal organizations.
Accordingly, HSI prioritized immigration enforcement over fentanyl-related criminal investigations,” the report found.
That also led to a reduction in fentanyl investigations and seizures.

title: Trump admin moving to revoke visas from potentially hundreds of thousands of asylum seekers
summary:
The Trump administration is moving to revoke visas from potentially hundreds of thousands of foreigners who have applied for or are seeking asylum in the United States.
It comes as the Trump administration has aggressively sought to both prevent immigrants from coming to the US and to remove those who are already in the country.
An immigration lawyer and a former State Department consular official described the planned deportations as largely symbolic and meant to play into the administration’s claims that the visa system is being abused.
Mackler told CNN that asylum seekers who have their visas revoked would “at a minimum” have to be given a hearing before an immigration judge before they could be deported.
The State Department announced earlier this month that it had revoked more than 175,000 visas since President Donald Trump began his second term, marking a significant jump from December.

title: Judge denies Minnesota's bid to compel the extradition of an ICE officer from Texas
summary:
BROWNSVILLE, Texas (AP) — A federal judge on Wednesday refused to order Texas to extradite an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer charged with shooting a man and lying about it during the immigration crackdown in Minneapolis.
U.S. District Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. wrote in an order that he couldn't prevent a county sheriff from releasing Christian Castro or order Texas Gov.
After a Minnesota judge issued a nationwide warrant for Castro's arrest in May, authorities, including Minnesota's Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, arrested Castro in Cameron County on May 29.
Under Texas law and barring extradition, Castro must be released after 90 days of detention, which is Thursday.
Advertisement AdvertisementThe judge said in his order that the extradition laws do not outline how long the Texas governor can take to make that decision.

title: Spain requests emergency funding from the EU over Ceuta migrants
summary:

Share Spain requests emergency funding from the EU over Ceuta migrants on social mediaSpain has formally requested emergency funding from the European Union to address the migration situation in its North African enclave of Ceuta, weeks after tens of thousands of people surged across the border from Morocco.
The Spanish government also took steps to speed up the return of the migrants who still remain in the Spanish territory of Ceuta.
Spanish authorities must identify those remaining in Ceuta to establish whether they are entitled to international protection or, if not, begin procedures for their return.
Ceuta and Melilla, Spain’s two North African enclaves, hold the EU’s only land borders with Africa.
